REGN.thesis_one_line: Diversified biotech (Dupixent, Eylea HD, growing oncology pipeline) priced for far less growth than it is likely to deliver, but Dupixent's 2031 patent cliff is a real, named risk.
kill_criteria: Legacy Eylea US net sales decline exceeds 50% YoY in any quarter through 2027
Dupixent global net sales growth falls below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters
Any Phase 3 readout failure or negative FDA action on the Factor XI anticoagulant program or the GIP/GLP-1 obesity asset
GAAP-to-non-GAAP EPS gap exceeds 25% for two consecutive quarters without a disclosed one-time driver
Net debt turns materially positive (>$3B) to fund an acquisition without a clearly accretive, disclosed rationale
key_adverse_facts: Legacy Eylea US net sales down ~45% YoY in Q2 2026 on biosimilar conversion; guided to keep declining sequentially low-to-mid-teens each quarter through 2026
GAAP diluted EPS ($12.23, Q2 2026) is ~17% below non-GAAP EPS ($14.29), driven mainly by mark-to-market swings on equity holdings, not operating performance
Dupixent (~40%+ of revenue) loses US patent exclusivity around 2031, a single-product concentration risk on the scale of the Eylea situation just observed
AERIFY-2 Phase 3 trial for itepekimab (COPD) missed its primary endpoint, a partial precedent for pipeline risk
data_conflicts: Quant snapshot's NTM P/E (15.29x) is self-flagged 'unreliable' due to thin/split analyst FY0-vs-FY1 coverage (ntm_quality: unreliable) — not relied on at face value
Yahoo-sourced beta field (0.19) looks anomalously low for a biotech and was not used in the WACC assumption (8% assumed instead)
REGN.confidence_in_thesis: medium — biosimilar/patent-cliff risk is real and quantified rather than eliminated; standard-depth pass left some gaps (FDA site-inspection database and insider Form-4 pattern not exhaustively checked)

RJF.thesis_one_line: Well-run wealth-management and investment-banking firm delivering on a stated 20% margin target; at 2.97x tangible book the price already pays for today's 22% ROTCE, so it is fairly priced rather than cheap.
kill_criteria: Adjusted pretax margin falls below 18% for two consecutive quarters
Net income falls below $450M in any quarter for two consecutive quarters
Raymond James Bank's standalone total capital ratio (per the 10-Q Regulatory Capital note, not the RJF-consolidated ratio) falls below 15%
The consolidated cash-sweep litigation results in a certified class and/or a disclosed reserve/settlement exceeding $250M
Parent-level debt (senior notes payable plus other borrowings, about $4.47B at 30 Jun 2026) rises above $5B without a clearly disclosed, accretive acquisition rationale
Adjusted return on tangible common equity below 17% for two consecutive quarters (22.0% in the first nine months of fiscal 2026)
key_adverse_facts: Q3 FY25 net income ($436M) was the weakest of the last nine quarters, reflecting softer capital-markets/investment-banking revenue that quarter
Consolidated cash-sweep class actions remain pending (partial dismissal March 2026, class-certification motion filed May 2026); financial exposure unresolved
Q3 FY26 non-compensation expense run-rate reflects 'two recent acquisitions' not named in the sources reviewed this pass

Correction (26 Sep 2026, DA7 fact-check confirmed vs the 2026-06-30 10-Q): Raymond James Bank standalone total capital ratio is 16.4% (Jun-26), up from 15.2% (Sep-25) -- only ~20bp above the 15% kill-criterion threshold nine months earlier, not the 22.5% RJF-consolidated figure originally cited; total parent-level debt is ~$4.47B (senior notes payable $3.52B + other borrowings $0.95B), not $0.7-0.95B as originally stated

RA13 (6 Oct 2026): at $159.87 the stock is 2.97x tangible book and 2.42x book; justified P/B at 18.1% ROE and 9.3% cost of equity is 2.40x - the price already pays for the whole ROE spread, and the base-case 3-year return (+6.5% a year) is below the cost of equity
RA13: Q3 FY26 effective tax rate was 20.7% (vs 23.1% for nine months) on non-taxable COLI gains; adjusted ROTCE of 23.5% is flattered by about 1 point
RA13: new director appointed (8-K 1 Sep), $0.54 dividend declared, August operating data furnished 23 Sep; no merger or guidance change
data_conflicts: None material identified this pass; b1 quant composite (0.504, decile 6) is more moderate than the triage's framing implies, driven by a strong earnings-momentum (SUE) score offsetting weaker value/momentum family scores
RJF.confidence_in_thesis: medium - guidance record and capital are primary-sourced, but the price (2.97x TBV) assumes the record 22% ROTCE persists, Q3 benefited from a 20.7% tax rate, and earnings are linked to record client assets ($1.97tn in August)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA13): the original reverse DCF capitalised net income as cash (RJF retains earnings to fund 13% bank-loan growth) at an 11.4% cost of equity built on rf 4.2% and ERP 5.5% (4.2% implied growth vs a 7-9% base). At rf 5.17%, ERP 4.14% and beta 1.0 the cost of equity is 9.3%; the like-for-like bank test is P/TBV 2.97x vs ROTCE: implied sustainable ROTCE 21.7% (19.4% at 8.5%, 23.8% at 10%) against 22.0% delivered (adjusted, nine months) and a 20% through-cycle base. In line (+1.7 points); justified P/TBV 2.70x at 20%, 3.02x at 22%. RJF has no row in V1.

RJF.scenario_basis: Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA13). From $159.87, TBV/share $53.74, 192.1m shares, dividend $2.16 growing 7%, payout 70-85% of net income to common. Bear: ROTCE 14%, exit 2.0x TBV. Base: ROTCE 20%, exit 2.7x. Bull: ROTCE 23%, exit 3.2x. Replaces -2% / +11% / +20%, which were not tied to a multiple or a return on equity.

SCHW.thesis_one_line: Largest US discount brokerage/custodian compounding fast post-TD-Ameritrade integration, but much of the recent growth is a NIM-recovery tailwind that will not repeat every year.
kill_criteria: Full-year net interest margin fails to reach the guided 3.00%–3.10% range for FY2026, or the guided Q4 2026 exit NIM of 3.25%–3.30% is not achieved
Accumulated AFS unrealized loss position rises back above $5B or above 10% of stockholders' equity
Long-term debt + capital lease obligations rise above $28B without a disclosed, NIM-accretive rationale
The cash-sweep litigation results in a certified class and/or a disclosed reserve/settlement exceeding $500M
Consolidated Tier 1 leverage ratio falls below 7.5%
key_adverse_facts: Long-term debt + capital lease obligations rose YoY ($20.2B to $22.7B) even as management describes reduced wholesale-funding use — an unreconciled tension

Active cash-sweep class action alleges sweep-cash economics helped finance the TD Ameritrade acquisition; SEC has broadened industry-wide scrutiny of cash-sweep programs (peer disclosures at Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo)
A material share of 2026 EPS acceleration is attributed by management itself to NIM recovery and reduced wholesale-funding cost — a partly non-repeatable tailwind, not purely durable organic growth
data_conflicts: None material identified this pass beyond the internal debt-growth-vs-'reduced-wholesale-funding' language noted above
SCHW.confidence_in_thesis: medium — strong, twice-raised guidance in 2026, but an uncertain share of the growth is mean-reversion rather than durable organic compounding, and cash-sweep litigation is unresolved
